meta.area_source: MapSPAM 2020 V2r2 rainfed maize harvested area
caveats: Pilot: every Kenyan county with rainfed maize, early-maturing maize sown at the FAO agricultural onset of each cell's forecast.

The Short Rains is the main maize season of the eastern counties only. In the western, Rift Valley, central and coastal counties most maize is grown in the Long Rains, often late-maturing varieties sown in March or April: there this map is the smaller Short Rains crop, not the county's main harvest (the county table gives each county's Short Rains share of its maize, HarvestStat).

Each 0.25° cell (about 28 km) is one field, grown by AquaCrop and by DSSAT, with the cell's average soil (SoilGrids), rain (CHIRPS and the bias-corrected forecast) and temperature (ERA5-Land; DSSAT also its radiation, humidity and wind): not any farmer's field.
Yields are water-limited, without nutrient stress, pests or management losses: read the percent of normal and the chances, not the tonnes per hectare.
A county is the mean of its cells, weighted by their rainfed maize area (MapSPAM 2020).
The normal is the same crop grown in the observed weather of 1993–2025; the terciles are those of 1993–2016.
The forecasts have not been verified against observed yields; the county normals are compared with HarvestStat's Short Rains maize yields (see the county table).
A crop sown into dry soil waits for rain to germinate, and its season counts from germination (a correction of AquaCrop-OSPy's end of season, November 2026).
